title: Second marriage during pendency of divorce - the legal consequences
p1:
A divorce case is pending… and someone decides to marry again. Is it just a personal choice, or can it create serious legal trouble?

Many people assume that filing for divorce means they are already free to start a new marriage. That assumption can be costly.
p2:
A pending divorce does not end a marriage. Until the divorce decree is granted, the first marriage legally continues. A second marriage during this period can be treated as an offence in many jurisdictions, including India, because the person may still be considered legally married.

The surprising part? Even if both spouses have agreed to separate, or the divorce process is taking years, the legal status does not change until the court officially dissolves the marriage.
p3:
The practical takeaway is simple: emotional separation and legal separation are not the same thing. Before entering a new marriage, confirm that the previous marriage has been legally ended and the final order has been issued.

A few minutes of legal verification can prevent years of complications, including criminal proceedings and disputes over the validity of the second marriage.
conclusion: Do you think people should be allowed to remarry once a divorce case is filed, or only after the court grants the final divorce decree?
